extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification containing 31,500 images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images per class, with spatial resolution varying from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel, extracted from Google Earth.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu (Northwestern Polytechnical University)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were extracted by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth (Google Inc.), covering more than 100 countries and regions all over the world. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Google Earth (Google Inc.), which maps the Earth by the superimposition of images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography and geographic information system (GIS) onto a 3D globe.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Scene classes were first selected by investigating existing datasets and searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar. Images were then extracted from Google Earth under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales. Each image was sized to 256×256 pixels in RGB color space.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Scene class labels were assigned by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation who extracted images from Google Earth.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset mainly covers images from Google Earth and may have lower spatial resolutions for certain classes (island, lake, mountain, and snowberg). The dataset was designed to have high within-class diversity and between-class similarity, including fine-grained scene classes with high semantic overlapping.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Almost all existing datasets including this one have limitations such as small scale of scene classes and image numbers, lack of image variations and diversity, and saturation of accuracy. The dataset covers only overhead imagery and does not incorporate ground-level photos or social media data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, testing, and benchmarking of remote sensing image scene classification methods, particularly deep learning-based approaches. It can also be used for geographic image retrieval and land use/land cover determination.

name.evidence: we propose a large-scale dataset, termed 'NWPU-RESISC45', which is a publicly available benchmark for REmote Sensing Image Scene Classification (RESISC), created by Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU).

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we first investigated all scene classes of the existing datasets to form 30 widely-used scene categories. Then, we searched the keywords of 'OBIA', 'GEOBIA', 'land cover classification', 'land use classification', 'geographic image retrieval', and 'geospatial object detection' on Web of Science and Google Scholar to carefully select 15 meaningful scene classes.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The spatial resolution varies from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel for most of the scene classes except for the classes of island, lake, mountain, and snowberg that have lower spatial resolutions.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: almost all existing datasets have a number of limitations, including the small scale of scene classes and the image numbers, the lack of image variations and diversity, and the saturation of accuracy.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The creation of this dataset will enable the community to develop and evaluate various data-driven algorithms. Finally, several representative methods are evaluated using the proposed dataset and the results are reported as a useful baseline for future research.
